To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the failure envelopes are highly conservative, (2) the failure envelope is not a unique function of the failure criterion, and (3) the failure envelope depends on the bone-implant interface conditions.

the failure envelope of the bone-implant system depends on the failure criterion used and on the implant geometry, that the failure envelope can be used to determine the maximum admissible load for the bone-implants system, that the maximum admissible loads are higher when the bone is considered to be a continuum than when it is considered to be an assemblage of trabeculae, and that the maximum admissable loads for the bone- implant system are higher than those of the implant alone

the failure envelope for the jawbone is determined by the bone remodeling criteria and the maximum strain criterion, and that the maximum stress and minimum strain criteria are conservative, while the minimum strain energy density criterion is nonconservative.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bone remodeling criterion is the most conservative of those considered, and that the failure envelopes are not significantly different from each other.
the bone failure criteria, which are based on the strain level, are more conservative than those that are based on stress levels.
the failure envelope concept is a powerful tool to assess the admissible loads for dental implants and their interaction with the jawbone.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the failure envelope concept provides a useful tool to compare the different failure criteria and to assess the influence of the different parameters.
a failure criterion based on the von Mises stress is most conservative, while the failure envelope based on the strain criterion is the least conservative.
a conservative failure envelope for the dental implant system can be constructed by combining the failure criteria of bone flow and bone fracture.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a strain-based criterion for jawbone failure is more restrictive than a stress-based one.
the failure criteria are not equivalent, and their choice has a significant impact on the resulting failure envelopes.
the admissible loads are not only a function of the implant geometry but are also dependent on the failure criterion used to define the failure envelope.
